whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Real
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Everyday Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, which can matter a great deal depending on how the injury affected your life.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, so you don't pay out of pocket up front — we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Del Rey Oaks?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file most personal injury claims. If the claim involves a government agency or public road, the window can be much shorter — sometimes just six months — so it's worth checking your situation promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for what happened. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Del Rey Oaks?
items.answer: Public collision records point to higher volumes along Canyon Del Rey Boulevard, Rt 68, General Jim Moore Boulevard, and Rt 218, with reported incidents tending to peak on Wednesdays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any road's safety.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. We provide free case reviews and don't charge you anything upfront. We work on contingency — we only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary California personal injury cases, there's no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. The amount depends on the specifics of your injury and how it affected your life, which we can evaluate with you.
